title: Notabene supports ISO 20022 for stablecoin payments
summary: Notabene now supports ISO 20022. Banks can send stablecoin payments in the format their payment teams already use, with counterparty verification and Travel Rule compliance on every payment.
body_markdown:
*Notabene now supports ISO 20022. Banks can send stablecoin payments in the format their payment teams already use, and map their existing payment flows directly to stablecoin rails with counterparty verification and Travel Rule compliance on every payment.*


## Stablecoin payments on existing banking rails


Banks have spent years orchestrating their payment flows using the[ISO 20022](https://notabene.id/glossary/iso-20022) standard. As they now build[stablecoin](https://notabene.id/glossary/stablecoin) payment products, a major hurdle is changing the underlying operations of these legacy payment flows to adopt new protocols and standards for digital asset transactions. This can lead to banks building separate integrations alongside the payments infrastructure they already run, with its own message formats, compliance processes, and operational overhead. Not only is it complex to map out initially, it is costly to maintain, with every new payment provider or counterparty presenting another integration to build and maintain.


With native ISO 20022 support, Notabene now enables banks to plug into stablecoin payment rails and the Notabene Network of 2,400+ counterparties across 115+ jurisdictions, all while maintaining the same payment messaging protocol used by the bank's existing payment workflows.


## How it works


A bank sends[pain.001](https://notabene.id/glossary/pain-001) payment instructions the same way it does today, with no custom translation needed. Notabene maps each instruction to the Transaction Authorization Protocol (TAP), an open messaging standard for digital asset payments, then identifies the counterparty institution, exchanges[Travel Rule](https://notabene.id/glossary/travel-rule) data with it, and runs the bank's own policies before the payment settles. The bank gets a[pain.002](https://notabene.id/glossary/pain-002) status report back for every instruction, so it can meet its Travel Rule obligations and run pre-transaction authorization workflows without changing how it structures its payment messages.


Payment details travel with the payment, including the beneficiary's account (such as an[IBAN](https://notabene.id/glossary/international-bank-account-number-iban) ), so the receiving institution knows who paid and why. When a payment passes through intermediaries, every leg and every party is authorized as part of one flow.


Your payment team never needs to handle wallet addresses, chains or crypto protocols. We handle the stablecoin, the chain and the messaging underneath, through the Transaction Authorization Protocol (TAP). Teams that want to work with digital assets directly still can.


Institutions pay each other directly. We connect them, verify the counterparty and keep the record, and we never hold or move the funds.


## For payment providers and digital asset infrastructure providers


In addition to benefiting the banks originating the payments,[payment service providers](https://notabene.id/glossary/payment-service-provider-psp) and digital asset infrastructure providers on the Notabene Network receive these payments as authorized stablecoin payments, with the counterparty and compliance data attached.


If you're a payment provider, you can process compliant payments from your banking partners as they arrive, without building ISO 20022 support or chasing counterparty data yourself. If you run custody or wallet infrastructure, your clients' ISO 20022 instructions arrive as authorized payments on the platform they already use with you.


## Start mapping your payment flows


[Talk to our team](https://notabene.id/sign-up-for-notabene?utm_source=notabene-blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=iso-20022-now-available) about mapping your payment flows to stablecoin payments, or book a demo to see how it works.


Developers can go deeper in our[ISO 20022 documentation](https://devx.notabene.id/v2.1/docs/iso-20022-v21) and[Payments API guide](https://devx.notabene.id/v2.1/docs/payments-v21) .


New to TAP? Read our glossary entry on the[Transaction Authorization Protocol (TAP)](https://notabene.id/glossary/transaction-authorization-protocol-tap) .
